title: Voxel Printing Anatomy: Design and Fabrication of Realistic, Presurgical Planning Models through Bitmap Printing
protocol: Open the medical image computing software.
Click the File button and select DICOM from the dropdown menu.
Wait for the DICOM Browser window to open.
In the DICOM Browser window, select Import.
Navigate to the DICOM file stack and click the Import button.
Ensure that the selected stack of DICOM files are loaded into the DICOM Browser.
Check that the data has been correctly populated in Patient, Study, Series, and Instance categories.
Click the Advanced check box to activate additional metadata options.
Select the desired Series Number and click Examine.
Ensure the desired sequence is not displaying any warnings.
Load the selected DICOM Data file by clicking its checkbox.
Select the highest resolution images with the thinnest slice acquisition for printing at 15 µm or 27 µm thickness.
Navigate to Modules and select Volume Rendering Module from the dropdown menu.
Select the name of the sequence from the Volume dropdown menu in the Volume Rendering module.
Click the Eye Ball icon next to the Volume dropdown to visualize the selected volume in 3D.
Navigate to the Advanced Tools by clicking the arrow next to Advanced.
Select the Volume Property tab to open a set of controls for modifying the color channel of the voxel model.
Left-click in the Scalar Opacity Mapping field to create points where intensity values will be defined by opacity.
Place points along the scale to visualize the anatomy of interest.
Navigate to the Scalar Color Mapping menu.
Left-click in the field to create points and specify colors correlated to intensity values.
Double-click in the field to open a Select Color window to modify color information.
Navigate to Modules and select the Segment Editor.
Ensure the Segment Editor toolbars appear.
Navigate to the Segmentation dropdown and select Create New Segmentation.
Type a custom name for the segmentation from the Rename Segmentation popup window and click OK.
Navigate to the Master Volume dropdown and select the active volume.
Click the Add button directly below the dropdown.
Ensure the segment container is created in the field below.
Select the Scissors tool from the Effects menu.
Select Fill Inside, Free-form, and Unlimited from the Scissors menu.
Hover over the 3D Window, right-click and hold while drawing around the area to be erased.
Repeat this process until all areas to be deleted are covered.
Select the Mask Volume tool from the Effects menu.
Check Select Inside to delete all image data covered by the segment.
Modify the Fill Value to -1000.
Hit apply.
Click the Eye Ball next to the Output Volume to show the new masked volume.
Navigate to Modules and select Volume Rendering from the dropdown menu.
Click the Eye Ball next to the active volume to turn off the visualization.
Select the newly created masked volume from the dropdown menu.
Click the Eye Ball to activate the volume.
Open the Properties dropdown menu under Inputs and select the Volume Property created in step 1.2.5.
Ensure the volume in the 3D View is masked and color-encoded.
Navigate to Modules, select Slicerfab from the dropdown.
Ensure the Print Parameters and Output Parameters menus are present.
Set X resolution to 600 DPI and Y resolution to 300 DPI under Printer Parameters dropdown.
Set Layer thickness to 27 µm.
Modify scale of the final model as needed in Output Parameters menu.
Select a file location for the slices to be saved and click Generate.
Navigate to File | Automate | Batch.
In the Batch popup window, select the action created in the previous step from the Action dropdown.
Under the Source menu, click the Choose button and navigate to the folder of images exported in step 3.1.3.
Under the Destination menu, click the Choose button, select a destination folder location for the new files, and click OK.
Open the print software.
Click Apps and Launch Voxel Print Utility from the dropdown menu.
In the Slice Files' Prefix text box, enter the prefix of the PNG file stack.
Next, click the Select button and navigate to the folder where the PNG files stack is located, and click OK.
Under Slice Range, ensure the First Slice and Number of Slices match the number of files in the created folder.
Under Slicing Parameters, ensure the Sliced thickness (mm) matches the settings specified in step 3.1.1.1.
Ensure Slice width (pixels) and Slice height (pixels) match the PNG files width and height.
Under Background Color, ensure the background matches the background color set not to print.
Once completed, click the Next button.
On the Tools page under Material Mapping, select the material from the dropdown menu to be mapped to the associated color.
Repeat this process for each color in the menu.
Click Finish | OK on the popup window Info Gcvf creation succeeded.
On the host computer print software, click File | Import File from the dropdown menu.
Navigate to the Gcvf file and click Load.
On the main screen, select Print.
